

| Matt  | Matt laid out that Trade Funding now operates across three areas: Commercial — the core business (comparison reports for business owners), the "hero" of the site Property & Personal (formerly Individuals/Consumer) — helping their commercial customers with personal funding needs (mortgages, personal loans, etc.) — grew out of referral opportunities, spearheaded by James Connect — the vendor-facing side, using the same QR code technology to let vendors help their customers get funded for goods/services Commercial Must Stay the Hero The commercial offering needs to remain the central focus. He's wary of diluting the brand by appearing to "do everything" — worried that spreading focus across all three pillars makes the company look like a generalist rather than a specialist. This directly shaped his skepticism toward flashy multi-pillar navigation. Navigation & Site Architecture Leaning toward something more like a top-bar "switch" mechanism (similar to how sites let you toggle between country/region sites) rather than equal-weighted nav buttons. URL structure: tradefunding.com.au as the main hub, with /individuals and a connect-specific path (e.g., "TradeConnect") as sub-sections — each pillar's marketing would funnel to its own extension. Wants simple, clear top-level navigation labels — questioning generic terms like "Products" or "About," preferring more action/benefit-oriented framing (e.g., "What funding do I need?" or "Offer funding/solutions" instead of just "Connect"). Bringing Back "Purpose-Driven" Navigation A recurring theme: Matt misses the old site's purpose-driven approach — letting customers navigate by "what do you want the money for?" rather than only by product type. He wants to reintroduce this dual pathway: Help customers figure out what they need (purpose-driven) Let customers who already know what they want go straight to products He feels the current/new site has more content and is structurally better than the old one, but may have lost this important customer-journey/context-setting element. Call-to-Action & Conversion Focus Matt's biggest structural concern: whether the site's value proposition is strong enough to drive people to "apply"/"proceed" from a navigation standpoint. He wants: Simple, direct CTAs (apply, proceed) A navigation experience where a customer instantly understands "this is what I thought this was about" upon landing Everything after that first impression should just be logical, easy-to-follow navigation to get where they need to go Practical/Tactical Decisions Contact info → move to footer (agreed with Jana); consider a floating contact button instead of top-nav placement Individuals & Connect should get basic placeholder landing pages for now (simple one-pagers) — not full builds — so all three pillars are represented while the main site structure gets finalized Connect's page/value prop is already largely built and just needs proper integration/navigation into the main site All three pillars must be part of the same project/site build (not separate efforts) — important because the vendor team needs the "individuals" and "connect" pages live soon (a trade show is driving urgency for a registration landing page) Underlying Tension He's Navigating Matt is weighing: "We are commercial, but we also help with X" — framing individuals/connect as things the company also does (an extension of trust from commercial), not separate identities competing for attention with the core brand. |

Goal is to keep that strength while making the breadth (business, property, personal finance) immediately clear to a first-time visitor. |
